## Redaction

Scanned every captured step output for 3 secret-named value(s) (`-e freeipa_client_sssd_password_expiry_policy`, `/home/kjelly/.vault/freeipa-ca-trust-sandbox.yaml:ipa_admin_password`, `/home/kjelly/.vault/freeipa-ca-trust-sandbox.yaml:ipa_dm_password`): **HITS**, the raw output must not be committed:

- step L3 check-mode dry-run: `-e freeipa_client_sssd_password_expiry_policy` × 2
- step L4 apply: `-e freeipa_client_sssd_password_expiry_policy` × 2
- step L6 idempotency: `-e freeipa_client_sssd_password_expiry_policy` × 2

## Failure paths and arms

Everything below ran on the same two VMs right after the chain above (state: `renew`, converged). Each arm is a separate `ansible-playbook playbooks/apply/freeipa-client-apply.yml -l pwexp-cli` run or a live SSH session from the controller, not part of the `topology test` chain. The SSH driver is a per-run scratch script (not committed): it generates every password in memory, sends it over stdin, and prints none. Test accounts: `pilot-pwchange` (keeps the `pilot-all` sudo rule) and `pilot-pwrefuse`, both with the run's SSH public key and no password until the driver resets it with the admin `ipa passwd` (an admin reset is expired at once, the same state as a roster default password). Fixture accounts were created by the chain before the client first asked SSSD about them; no `sss_cache` or restart was used to make any result appear.

| Arm | Setting | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A03 valid password | `renew` | `pilot-pwvalid`, key login: shell, rc 0 |
| A04 expired, user knows the old password | `renew` | `ssh -tt` with the key: sshd printed "WARNING: Your password has expired. You must change your password now and login again!", ran `passwd` (Current Password, New password, Retype), `passwd: password updated successfully`, then disconnected without a shell. FreeIPA `krbPasswordExpiration` moved from `20261105093312Z` (expired at reset) to `20270203093317Z` (+90 days). Re-login with the key then gave a shell and `sudo -n true` succeeded. The first two re-login attempts, 0.3 s and 1.5 s after `passwd` ended, were still refused with rc 1 (message not captured); the third, at 2.9 s, succeeded. A user who reconnects within about 3 s of the change can be refused once more |
| A05 wrong old password | `renew` | "Password change failed. Server message: Old password not accepted." / "passwd: password unchanged", no shell |
| A05 cancel at the prompt | `renew` | Ctrl-C at "Current Password:" did not close the session; the driver killed ssh after its 20 s timeout. No shell was reached |
| A05 terminal dropped mid-prompt | `renew` | ssh killed at the prompt; afterwards the account is still expired and still gets no shell |
| A08 BatchMode, no TTY | `renew` | rc 1, "Password change required but no TTY available.", the remote command did not run |
| A09 remote command / sftp | `renew` | command not executed (marker file absent on the client), rc 1; `sftp` rc 255 "Connection closed" |
| A17 key-only account | `renew` | `pilot-nopw` key login refused; sshd journal: `pam_sss(sshd:account): Access denied for user pilot-nopw: 4 (System error)` |
| A13 `--check --diff` | `warn` over `renew` | `changed=0`; sssd.conf md5 and sssd start time unchanged |
| A13 `--tags C13` | `warn` | `changed=2`, SSSD restarted; confdb and file both `expire, pwd_expire_policy_warn` |
| A02 near expiry | `warn` | `pilot-pwnear` key login: shell plus "Your password will expire in 2 days."; `pilot-pwrefuse` (expired) key login: shell |
| A14 `off` | `off` | `changed=2`, then `changed=0` on rerun; `ipa_access_order = expire`; `pilot-pwrefuse` (expired) and `pilot-nopw` (no password) key logins both give a shell |
| A01 unset | unset | `changed=0`; sssd.conf md5 and sssd start time identical before and after |
| A11 duplicate `ipa_access_order` | `renew` | refused before any change ("not in a shape this playbook edits safely"), rescue ran, sssd.conf md5 identical, SSSD not restarted, active |
| A11 unknown option in sssd.conf | `renew` | `sssctl config-check` rc 1, rescue restored the snapshot, md5 identical to before the run, SSSD active |

Other findings from this run:

- The Redaction section reports HITS for `-e freeipa_client_sssd_password_expiry_policy`: the scanner treats any input whose name contains "password" as a secret, so the harmless value `renew` was redacted in the captured output (it also shows in the title as `<redacted>`). No secret was involved; the contract declares this input `secret: false`.
- An earlier development-only run on other VMs showed that a sudo rule attached to a user after SSSD had already looked the user up was not visible on the client for a while (`sudo -l -U` said "not allowed"). That is the sudo-cache behaviour (A16) and not part of this feature. The test accounts are now created before the client enrolls, which avoids it.

## Not covered / limits

- Only `renew` ran inside the `topology test` chain; `warn`, `off`, unset and the negative controls are separate runs on the converged VMs, so they have no L3/L6 chain of their own.
- Not run: A06 (disabled account, `krbPrincipalExpiration`, HBAC deny), A07 (login-probe canary; `login-probe` was not deployed), A10 (gateway, directory, target-policy hosts; `renew` is refused there by the preflight and that gate was tested only by group membership), A12 (FreeIPA primary down, replica, offline cache), A16 (sudo cache crossing with password expiry).
- One server (AlmaLinux 9) and one Ubuntu 24.04 client; Ubuntu 22.04, EL9 clients and Ubuntu 26.04 are out of scope. Ubuntu 22.04 rejection was exercised only by overriding the fact in a development run.
- The 3-second re-login window after a password change was seen once per run and its refusal text was not captured.
- The SSH driver is not committed, so the A-row results above are operator observations, not machine-generated parts of the record.
